summary: AP2 moves no money, so payment law reaches it through the parties that use mandates: issuers, Credential Providers, processors and merchants. Its main legal value is evidence: a signed record of what the user authorized, which is the central fact in any unauthorized-transaction dispute under Regulation E, Regulation Z, PSD2 or the UK PSRs. Open questions are whether an open mandate counts as consent to each later transaction, how strong customer authentication works when the user is absent, and who carries the loss when an agent stays inside its limits but misreads the user. Within Visa's system, Visa's rules put an agent's errors on the cardholder, who is responsible for an Agentic Payment Provider's actions as if the cardholder had initiated them. Those rules yield to applicable law. The specification claims no compliance with any of these rules.

rows.text: Regulation E treats a transfer as unauthorized only without actual authority, and excludes transfers by someone the consumer gave the access device to until notice. An open AP2 mandate is evidence of authority given to an agent, which may shift losses toward the consumer.

Regulation Z caps cardholder liability for unauthorized use at 50 dollars and asks whether there was actual, implied or apparent authority. Whether an agent acting outside a mandate has apparent authority is open; mandates are the evidence either way.
No federal statute or CFPB rule on AI agents in payments was found; Senator Warner asked Treasury on 2026-06-02 to examine liability for agentic payment rails.
AP2 has no KYC, sanctions or know-your-agent layer. AML and sanctions duties stay with the Credential Provider, processor and network that already carry them.
Regulation P governs how financial institutions share consumer financial information; risk_data and disclosed mandate fields reaching a Credential Provider fall under the provider's existing duties.

The RTS on strong customer authentication requires two factors and dynamic linking of amount and payee for remote payments. The AP2 glossary defines both terms but the spec claims no compliance; a human-not-present payment needs an exemption, a merchant-initiated setup or a delegated model.
PSD2 requires payer consent to the specific transaction and caps payer liability for unauthorized ones. Whether a signed open mandate is consent to each later transaction is untested.
PSD3 and the Payment Services Regulation reached provisional agreement on 2025-11-27 and were not in the Official Journal in the latest sources found; no agent-specific provisions were reported.
AI Act transparency duties under Article 50 apply from 2026-08-02; the Digital Omnibus moved Annex III high-risk duties to 2027-12-02. A shopping or payment agent is not high-risk by default.
GDPR Article 22 limits decisions based solely on automated processing with significant effects. AP2 makes selective disclosure of constraints mandatory, which supports data minimization.
The Payment Services Regulations 2017 treat a payment as authorised only with payer consent (regulation 67) and cap liability at 35 GBP for misappropriated instruments (regulation 77).

The FCA said on 2026-03-25 it will consider whether regulation must change for agentic payments, and HM Treasury consulted from 2026-07-14 to 2026-10-06 on authentication, consent and liability for agents.
The Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 amends UK GDPR rules on automated decision-making.
The Retail Payment Activities Act has required payment service providers to have risk management and safeguarding frameworks since 2025-09-08. No agent-specific liability rule was found.
PIPEDA governs private-sector personal information, including risk_data and disclosed mandate fields held by Canadian parties.
The MAS E-Payments User Protection Guidelines allocate liability for unauthorized and erroneous e-payments.
MAS issued Guidelines on AI Risk Management on 2026-10-07, effective 2027-10-07, and names agentic AI systems.

Visa's rules govern Visa and its member institutions and yield to applicable law. Since 2025-10-18 they have required an Agentic Payment Provider to enroll in Visa Intelligent Commerce and register with Visa, directly or via an Agentic Payment Enabler. Within Visa's system, they make the cardholder responsible for the provider's actions in an Agentic Transaction as if the cardholder had initiated it. A merchant must not require a cardholder to waive the right to dispute such a transaction.

Visa calls none of its agent rules a liability shift and adds no agent-specific dispute condition or fee; its April 2026 US interchange schedule has no agentic category. It does require issuers to pay for Agentic Transactions made under a cardholder's payment instructions and not to block them wholesale. From 2026-10-24 it also accepts an Agentic Payment Provider's login ID among the evidence that can defeat a card-absent fraud dispute. Worldpay (2026-07-30) says no liability shift exists yet for agentic transactions. AP2 itself leaves liability to the networks and offers mandates as evidence.

Mastercard says standard chargeback rights apply to agentic transactions. The 2026-06-02 Mastercard Rules add no agent-specific liability rule. They require pass-through wallet operators and checkout facilitators in Agent Pay to follow the Mastercard Agent Pay Program Standards. A web search on 2026-10-19 found no public copy of those standards.

On 2026-09-10 Ant International, Mastercard and Visa announced they will explore common Know Your Agent principles across their protocols, including TAP and Verifiable Intent; it is a collaboration, not a rule.
EMVCo published a draft agentic payments framework on 2026-09-01 and lists agentic transaction indicators as possible future work.
